policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'who was called Iscariot' renders either the simplex or the compound participle identically; nothing in the English or the notes distinguishes them.

Pure word order of pronoun and object; English 'deliver him unto them' fixes its own order regardless of the Greek sequence. The mapped note is alternative_rendering ('Or, betray') and cannot decide a reading.
Word order only; 'deliver him unto them in the absence of the multitude' renders either sequence. Both mapped notes are alternative_rendering.
Bare relative versus relative with preposition; ASV 'on which the passover must be sacrificed' supplies the English preposition either way.
Deliberative subjunctive versus future indicative; ASV 'Where wilt thou that we make ready?' renders both identically.
ASV 'the house whereinto he goeth' uses a directional relative answering the accusative construction, revising the KJV's locative 'where he entereth in' which renders the adverb.
ASV 'as he had said unto them' is a pluperfect, answering the pluperfect form and not the perfect of the alternative.
ASV reads 'and the apostles with him' with no numeral; the alternative adds 'twelve', which the English does not carry.
ASV 'I shall not eat it' carries no 'any more'; the alternative's added adverb would be rendered, as the KJV's 'I will not any more eat thereof' shows.
ASV 'I shall not eat it' renders a plain accusative object; the alternative's partitive prepositional phrase would give 'eat thereof' as in the KJV.
Prepositional phrase versus bare dative reflexive; ASV 'divide it among yourselves' renders either.
Added recitative conjunction, regularly left untranslated before direct speech; ASV 'for I say unto you, I shall not drink' is compatible with either.
ASV 'I shall not drink from henceforth' renders the temporal phrase that the alternative omits.
Two forms of the same relative in the temporal clause; ASV 'until the kingdom of God shall come' renders either.

Both candidates contain the same words of 19b-20, which ASV prints in full with the mapped textual_variant note recording that some authorities omit them. The candidates differ only in editorial bracketing, which no English wording can register.
Word order of the adverb and the noun phrase; 'And the cup in like manner after supper' is a free rendering available to either sequence.
ASV opens 'For the Son of man indeed goeth' with a causal conjunction, revising the KJV's 'And truly'; the alternative's connective is the copulative.
Word order of verb and adverbial phrase; English syntax puts 'goeth, as it hath been determined' in that order under either reading.
Present versus aorist imperative of the same verb; ASV 'let him become as the younger' renders either aspect.
Word order of copula and prepositional phrase; 'I am in the midst of you' is fixed by English syntax. The mapped notes are greek_gloss on 'sitteth at meat' and touch nothing here.
Two spellings of the same subjunctive; ASV 'that ye may eat' renders either.
ASV 'at my table in my kingdom' renders the prepositional phrase that the alternative omits.
ASV 'and ye shall sit on thrones' is a future indicative in an independent clause, which excludes the present form of r01; the two future forms are rendered alike and remain open.

All three candidates have the numeral, which ASV renders as 'the twelve tribes'; they differ only in whether the participle precedes or follows its object, and English requires 'judging the twelve tribes' in that order either way.
ASV begins 'Simon, Simon, behold' with no speech frame; the alternative's 'And the Lord said' is absent from the English.
Two spellings of the same aorist imperative; ASV 'establish thy brethren' renders either.
Future indicative with simple negative versus subjunctive with emphatic negative; ASV 'the cock shall not crow this day' renders either negated form.
ASV 'until thou shalt thrice deny' renders the terminal conjunction; the alternative means 'before', which is what the KJV printed ('before that thou shalt thrice deny').
Order of the pronoun, verb and infinitive, plus a redundant negative the English would not show; 'deny that thou knowest me' renders either.
ASV 'And he said unto them' carries no inferential particle, revising the KJV's 'Then said he unto them'; the alternative is the inferential conjunction ASV renders 'therefore' or 'then'.
Aorist imperative versus future indicative; 'let him sell his cloak' renders both, as the KJV's identical wording over the future form shows.
Aorist imperative versus future indicative; 'and buy a sword' renders both, as the KJV's identical wording over the future form shows.
ASV 'this which is written must be fulfilled in me' has no 'yet'; the alternative adds that adverb.
ASV 'that which concerneth me hath fulfilment' is singular; the alternative's neuter plural article would give 'the things concerning me'.
ASV 'and the disciples also followed him' has no possessive; the alternative adds 'his'.

ASV punctuates 'if thou be willing, remove this cup from me' as a conditional followed by an imperative; the alternative's infinitive complements the verb of willing, giving 'if thou be willing to remove this cup'.
Position of the demonstrative before or after the noun; 'this cup' in English either way.
Present versus aorist imperative of the same verb; 'but thine, be done' renders either aspect.

Both candidates contain the whole of verses 43-44, which ASV prints with the mapped textual_variant note that many authorities omit them. The candidates differ only in editorial marking, which the English cannot register.
Presence of the article after the preposition; ASV 'an angel from heaven' is the same under either. The mapped note concerns the omission of the whole passage, not this word.
Two equivalent connectives with the same verb; ASV 'and his sweat became' renders either.
Word order of pronoun and participle; 'found them sleeping' is fixed by English syntax.
ASV opens 'While he yet spake' with no connective, revising the KJV's 'And while he yet spake'; the alternative adds that particle.
Order of name, article and particle; 'But Jesus said unto him' renders either.
ASV 'they said, Lord, shall we smite' has no indirect object; the alternative adds 'unto him'.
Word order of the genitive and its head noun; 'the servant of the high priest' is fixed by English. The mapped note is a greek_gloss on 'servant'.
Position of the possessive pronoun; 'his right ear' is fixed by English word order.
ASV 'he touched his ear' can render the added pronoun or the bare article, which ASV routinely gives possessive force; the English does not distinguish them.
Presence of the article with the proper name, which English cannot show; 'And Jesus said' either way.
Aorist versus perfect of the same verb; ASV's 'Are ye come out' serves for both.
Word order of copula and pronoun; 'this is your hour' is fixed by English syntax.
English requires an object for 'brought him into the high priest's house' whether or not the pronoun stands in the Greek, so the added pronoun is not distinguished.
Two nouns both rendered 'house'; the English does not distinguish them.
Compound versus simplex participle, both 'had kindled a fire'; nothing in the English distinguishes them.
Added pronoun subject of a genitive absolute, already implied by 'and had sat down together'.
Predicate adjective versus prepositional phrase, both rendered 'in the midst of them'.
ASV 'But he denied, saying' has no object, revising the KJV's 'And he denied him'; the alternative adds that pronoun.
Position of the vocative, which English freely fronts; 'Woman, I know him not' does not fix the Greek order, and r00 differs from r01 only in punctuation.
Two verbs of speaking, both 'said'; the English does not distinguish them.
Two nouns both rendered 'word'; ASV 'the word of the Lord' is compatible with either.
ASV 'Before the cock crow this day' renders the temporal adverb that the alternative omits.
ASV 'And he went out, and wept bitterly' has a pronoun subject; the alternative names Peter.
The mapped greek_gloss note 'Greek him.' stands against 'Jesus' in 'the men that held Jesus', reporting that the Greek has the pronoun and not the proper name of the alternative.
ASV 'they blindfolded him, and asked him' lacks the alternative's clause about smiting his face.
ASV 'both chief priests and scribes' renders the correlative particle that the alternative omits.
ASV 'they led him away into their council' renders the prefix of the base verb, against the alternative's 'led up' which the KJV rendered simply 'led him into'.
ASV 'and if I ask you' has no adjunctive adverb; the alternative adds one, giving 'and if I also ask you'.
ASV ends 'ye will not answer'; the alternative adds 'me, nor let me go', which the English does not carry.
ASV 'But from henceforth' renders the adversative particle that the alternative omits, where the KJV has none.
Word order of verb, noun and object; 'What further need have we of witness?' renders either sequence.
